cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's tax machine prepare W-2s for HANGS: the yearly pay statement each employee gets.
First, it adds up the year's four quarterly payroll returns.
Next, the year's payroll: 101 employees and 27 pay runs. One new employee has no Social Security number on file yet.
Now it checks the IRS rules online. Eleven checks are confirmed; one question is left for a person.
Then it fills in each W-2. Box 1 is taxable pay; box 2 is income tax withheld. Boxes 3 to 6 are Social Security and Medicare wages and tax. Box 12 codes extras, like 401(k) savings.
Twelve checks pass: the W-2 totals match the four quarterly returns exactly.
Last, it writes the draft forms and their workpapers.

All done. 101 draft W-2s report just under $11.2 million of wages in box 1. Five items stay open: personal use of two company pickups to add to pay, 13 cents of Social Security tax to refund, a missing Social Security number, a check on overtime, and the filing itself. A person reviews and e-files by February 1; nothing is filed yet.
